s01: Some joints you don't glue at all. You cut fingers on one piece and matching slots on the other, and they press together. Everything about that joint comes down to one number: the thickness of your material. Measure it with calipers rather than trusting the label. Plywood sold as three millimetres often measures a little under, and the laser takes a little more as it cuts. So draw your slots at the thickness you measured, and cut a small test piece first. If the fit is loose, take a tenth of a millimetre off the slot and cut the test again. Once the test fits, everything you cut from that sheet will fit too. And because the joint is dimensioned from that one number, changing it changes the joint.
